newsitem.title: USA: Briefing on Korea talks likely at month's end.
newsitem.headline: Briefing on Korea talks likely at month's end.

text.p: A U.S.-South Korean briefing for North Korean officials on proposed four-party talks over the future of the Korean peninsula is expected to take place towards the end of January, the State Department said Friday.
But a meeting Thursday of U.S. and North Korean officials failed to pin down details of the meeting, spokesman Nicholas Burns told a news briefing.
David Straub, deputy director of the State Department's Korea Office, met officials from North Korea's U.N. mission in New York.
"Arrangements for the upcoming joint briefing on the four-party talks are under discussion, and I think the joint briefing will probably be held towards the end of this month," Burns said.
"What we need to work out with the North Koreans is where that will take place, who will attend, and a specific date. We don't have that worked out yet," he added.
The four-party talks were first proposed last April by U.S. President Bill Clinton and South Korean President Kim Young-sam.
Pyongyang has so far been non-committal on the talks, which would involve the two Koreas, the United States and China.
Relations between North and South Korea were chilled by the intrusion of a North Korean submarine into South Korean waters last September.

But a North Korean statement of regret nearly two weeks ago over that incident has cleared the way for progress on other issues, including the four-party talks, food aid to North Korea and supply of new nuclear reactors to Pyongyang.
